liquidity_buffer_sizing.text:
`contingency_funding_plan_trigger` answers "have any of our early-warning metrics fallen below their minimum acceptable levels, so the Contingency Funding Plan should be activated?" You give it `metrics` (current values) and `thresholds` (minimums). It flags each metric that is below its threshold and returns the list of breaches plus an activation decision. It is a logical yes/no test, not an arithmetic formula.

`liquidity_buffer_sizing` answers "how large should our liquidity buffer be?" It takes `stressed_net_outflows` per period, finds the deepest point of the cumulative outflow trough, and can add a management margin through `confidence_buffer`.

So one is a monitoring trigger that says whether to act, and the other is a sizing calculation that says how much liquidity to hold.

explain.text: `contingency_funding_plan_trigger` (Contingency Funding Plan Trigger) checks whether any liquidity early-warning metrics have fallen far enough to activate a contingency funding plan. You give it `metrics`, a mapping of each metric name to its current value, and `thresholds`, a mapping of each name to its minimum acceptable value. A metric counts as breached when its value is below its threshold, so lower means worse, as with LCR or survival days. It returns the list of breached triggers and a CFP activation decision, which is activated if any single metric is breached. It is a logical comparison rather than an arithmetic formula.

when.text:
The Contingency Funding Plan Trigger (`contingency_funding_plan_trigger`) fits when you want to test early-warning liquidity metrics against activation thresholds:

- You track metrics where lower means worse, such as LCR or survival days, and want to know whether any has fallen below its minimum acceptable value.
- You need a clear decision on whether the contingency funding plan is activated, plus the list of breached triggers.
- You have a named set of current values (`metrics`) and a matching set of minimum values (`thresholds`) to compare side by side.
- If what you need is the survival horizon itself, `survival_horizon_calculator` is listed as computing the days until cumulative net outflow exhausts HQLA, which could then feed in as one of your metrics.
